gaps.sentence: Don't rush — we've got ___ of time.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ of time (no article needed)
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of time' needs no article; 'lot of time' would need 'a', and 'much of time' needs 'the'.

gaps.sentence: We haven't got ___ chairs for everyone.
gaps.explanation: 'Enough chairs' means a sufficient number; 'too' before the noun would give the wrong meaning and position.

gaps.sentence: Some metals are magnetic; ___ are not.
gaps.explanation: 'Some ... others ...' contrasts unspecified groups; 'the others' would need a closed, known set.

gaps.sentence: There is so ___ crime in this area that people are afraid.
gaps.explanation: 'So much' is used with uncountable nouns like crime; 'plenty' would need 'of'.

gaps.sentence: Don't worry, we still have ___ time before the gates close.
gaps.hint: positive meaning: there is some time; 'time' is uncountable
gaps.explanation: 'A little time' means some time, which reassures; 'time' is uncountable.

gaps.sentence: Three of the six books were mine; ___ were my sister's.
gaps.hint: the defined remainder of a set of six
gaps.explanation: 'The others' refers to the specific remaining books in the known set of six.

gaps.sentence: A large ___ of students have applied this year.
gaps.explanation: 'A large number of students' is used with countable plurals; 'amount' is for uncountables.

gaps.sentence: ___ the students passed with good grades.
gaps.explanation: Before 'the + noun' use 'most of': 'Most of the students'; 'most the students' is wrong.
